dial.summary: 10Y Treasury at 5.32–5.35% (24-year highs) and DXY edging to 102.25 keep macro headwinds intact, but BTC.D holds firm at 58.5%, the 2s10s curve steepens to +55bps, and perp funding near 0.007% per 8h signals spot-led accumulation remains intact — September CPI (Oct 14) is the dominant near-term catalyst that will determine whether real yields and DXY can reverse course before the Oct 27–28 FOMC.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: G4 M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) at ~$103.6T based on StreetStats snapshot as of October 6, 2026 ($103,649B); US M2 $23.3T as of August 2026 (BusinessStats); 3-month constant-FX G4 change +0.87% to August 31; 4-week trend flat: no confirmed September G4 data (6–8 week reporting lag); YoY still positive (not contracting); status neutral — confirmed rising 4-week trend required for supportive; next G4 M2 update expected mid-November 2026.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: September 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI = 54.5%, released October 1 (most recent release; November ISM release November 3, 2026); 4-week trend flat: August 54.6% → September 54.5% = −0.1pp, within flat threshold; New Orders Index 55.3%, Production Index 56.7%, Prices Index 77.9% (highest since mid-2021); status neutral (above 50 but not rising on 4-week basis; supportive requires above 50 AND rising); next ISM Manufacturing release November 3, 2026.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY spot at 102.25–102.26 on October 7–8, 2026 (Investing.com historical table; up from 102.02 on Oct 6); 52-week high 102.54 set Oct 5; 4-week trend up: ~99.9 (Sep 5) → 102.25 (Oct 8) = +2.35% over 30 days, well above flat threshold; status headwind (above 100 threshold); DXY near 18-month high driven by 10Y yields at 5.32–5.35% (24-year highs) and safe-haven USD bid; FRED DTWEXBGS (broad index) not directly accessible this run but correlates closely with ICE DXY and confirms uptrend; October 14 CPI is the next major DXY repricing catalyst; a sustained close below 100 required for neutral status.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: FRED DFII10 (10-year TIPS constant maturity) at 2.92% as of October 2, 2026 (latest confirmed FRED reading); StreetStats Treasury par real yield 2.90% as of October 6; with 10Y at 5.32–5.35% and 10Y breakeven inflation at 2.36% (FRED T10YIE Oct 7), derived real yield ~2.96–2.99%; 4-week trend up: ~2.50% (Sep 3) → 2.92% (Oct 2) = +42bps; status headwind (rising 4-week trend AND above 2% threshold both met); breakeven at 2.36% signals elevated inflation expectations consistent with ISM Prices at 77.9%; October 14 CPI is the key repricing catalyst.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: October 7, 2026: 10Y Treasury at 5.32% (FXStreet; intraday touched 5.35%), 2Y at 4.77% (Treasury par yield per stockmarketwatch) → 2s10s spread = +0.55% (+55bps); 4-week trend up (steepening): Sep 5 spread ~+42bps → Oct 7 +55bps = +13bps steepening over 30 days, above the 5bps flat threshold; status supportive (positive and steepening — both criteria met); steepening driven by 10Y rising faster than 2Y as long-end absorbs fiscal/inflation premium; 10Y at 24-year high supports further bear steepening; October 14 CPI and October 27–28 FOMC are the next major yield curve catalysts.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6,743,031M ($6.74T) for week ending September 30, 2026 (Federal Reserve H.4.1 released October 1; most recent confirmed reading); October 8 H.4.1 release (week ending October 7) was scheduled for today at 4:30 PM ET but was not accessible at time of this run; 4-week trend flat: Sep 2 $6,737,204M → Sep 30 $6,743,031M = +$5.8B (+0.09%), marginal expansion within flat threshold on a $6.74T base; status supportive (holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau; no QT acceleration); weak September NFP (+29K) raises odds of a Fed hold at October 27–28 FOMC, supporting balance sheet stability; next confirmed data point from today's H.4.1 covering Oct 7.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate at approximately 0.0067% per 8h (MacroMicro, September 30, 2026; BTC/USD ~$84,602); Kraken perp rate 7.517% annualized (CF Benchmarks Sep 29) = ~0.0069% per 8h, consistent; 4-week trend up: ~0.003% per 8h (Sep 3 early-month) → ~0.0067% (Sep 30) = rising longs paying shorts but well-controlled; status supportive (0.0067% is well below the 0.04% overheating threshold — confirms spot-driven accumulation, not leveraged speculation); open interest rose to 653,000 BTC ($56.2B) from 626,000 BTC on Sep 30 (CoinDesk); October 14 CPI and October 27–28 FOMC are the next potential funding regime shift catalysts.

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$300–303B (DeFiLlama/CoinGecko early October 2026); total crypto market cap ~$2.9T (Oct 1–4 trackers); stablecoin dominance ~10.3–10.5% (arithmetic: $300–303B / $2.9T); BTC.D 58.5% (tv-hub.org Oct 2026); 30-day trend flat: ~10.4% (Sep 5) → ~10.4% (Oct 8) = negligible change; status neutral (not falling on 30-day basis = not supportive; total crypto rising but dominance not falling = headwind condition not met); USDT holds ~60% stablecoin market share; ~$300B in sidelined capital available to deploy if macro improves; October 14 CPI is the next stablecoin inflow/outflow catalyst.

upcoming.title: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment (October 2026 Preliminary)
upcoming.note: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment preliminary reading for October 2026 at 10:00 AM ET; September final was ~69.1; provides early Q4 consumer confidence read; with 10Y yields at 5.35% (24-year highs), DXY at 102.25, and September NFP at +29K, a weak print below 65 would reinforce risk-off sentiment; 1-year and 5-year inflation expectations sub-components are closely watched given ISM Prices at 77.9% — Fed is sensitive to second-round inflation anchoring.

upcoming.title: CPI (September 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Consumer Price Index for September 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — the dominant macro catalyst before the October 27–28 FOMC decision; August CPI YoY was +3.4–3.5%; ISM Manufacturing Prices Index at 77.9% (highest since mid-2021) is a leading signal for CPI upside; a hot print above +3.5% YoY could revive October hike odds, push DXY above 104, and test BTC below $80K; a dovish miss below +3.0% YoY would cement Fed hold expectations and likely catalyze DXY below 100 and a BTC breakout above $90K; real yields at 2.92% and DXY at 102.25 make this the single most important data point of the month.

upcoming.title: PPI (September 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Producer Price Index for September 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — pipeline inflation released the day after CPI; August PPI Final Demand was +2.8% YoY; ISM Manufacturing Prices at 77.9% is a leading signal of potential PPI upside; a hot PPI following a hot CPI would reinforce October hike expectations and likely drive DXY back above 103; triple-release morning (also Retail Sales and Jobless Claims) capable of generating significant volatility 12 days before October 27–28 FOMC.

upcoming.title: Retail Sales (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Census Bureau Retail Sales for September 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — released alongside September PPI and Initial Jobless Claims; given the September NFP shock (+29K), a weak retail sales print would confirm broad economic softening and reinforce Fed hold narrative; a strong print alongside weak labor would extend the late-cycle bifurcation signal — resilient consumer spending despite softening employment; provides pre-FOMC context on Q3 consumer demand ahead of the October 29 GDP advance estimate.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended October 11, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for the week ended October 11, 2026 — second consecutive weekly claims read post the September NFP shock; released alongside PPI and Retail Sales, making October 15 the most data-dense morning before the October 27–28 FOMC; a second consecutive above-200K print would confirm labor market softening is sustained; claims trajectory directly informs market odds for a Fed pause vs. hike at the October meeting.
